title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 14-16): X' is a curve or orbifold-type space. X~' is its universal covering with deck group π_1. J (written I on the previous page) is a set of base points, so Π_1 = Π_1(X';J) is the fundamental groupoid with object set J. A group G' (Galois or mapping-class type) acts, and this action is encoded by an extension 1→π_1→E'→G'→1 acting on X~'(J) = ⊔_j X~'(j), the fibres of the universal cover over the base points.

On the previous page, Grothendieck noted that the universal cover based at j is canonically X~'[j] ≅ X~'(j) ∧_{π_1} X~', with the choice of a point ξ removed.

On this page he defines the morphisms of the groupoid as Hom_{Π_1}(j,j') := Isom_covers(X~'[j], X~'[j']) and identifies this with Isom of right π_1-torsors X~'(j) → X~'(j'). Path composition becomes composition of torsor isomorphisms. So the connected groupoid Π_1 is rebuilt purely from the set X~'(J) with its free right π_1-action: objects are the orbits J = X~'(J)/π_1, and arrows are torsor isomorphisms between fibres.

He then rebuilds the G'-action on Π_1.
- On objects it is the action of G' on J induced by E' (π_1 acts trivially on orbits).
- On arrows, for g in G', take the fibre B_g = (image inverse of g under E'→G'), which is a π_1-bitorsor under left and right translation.
- The E'-action gives isomorphisms X~'(gj) ≅ X~'(j) ∧_{π_1} B_g.
- Hence a torsor isomorphism u: X~'(j)→X~'(j') yields u ∧ id_{B_g}: X~'(gj)→X~'(gj'). This is the arrow g_{Π_1} (the next page says 'd'où aussitôt la flèche envisagée').

The aim, made explicit on the next page, is an equivalence between two categories:
- (extension 1→π→E→G→1, nonempty E-set Z on which π acts freely);
- (connected groupoid Π with universal covering, G acting on Π by automorphisms).

This is a discrete or combinatorial dictionary for 'Galois action on the fundamental groupoid with several base points'. It is used in the Teichmüller-tower and 'paradigm' programme for curves, where the arithmetic or modular group acts on groupoids based at several (e.g. tangential) base points.
errors: Variance or convention slip: by Yoneda, Isom of covers X~'[j]→X~'[j'] is naturally Π_1(j',j) (contravariant) unless suitable conventions are fixed. Since Grothendieck writes it as a definition ('df'), this only affects the orientation (groupoid vs opposite groupoid).
Left/right bookkeeping: E' must act on the right of X~'(J) for X~'(j)∧_{π_1}B_g to land over gj with G' acting on the left of J, or else one should use B_{g^{-1}}. This is not specified and is minor.
Notation inconsistency: the index set is I on the previous page and J here. The subscript in 'Isom_{Π_1,f}' is unclear.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid on a set of base points, with morphisms as isomorphisms of fibre torsors of the universal cover (fibre-functor description).
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid via fibre functors / torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 Exp. V); R. Brown for groupoids with several base points
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. V (fibre functors, groupoid of paths); Esquisse d'un programme (several base points)

ideas.what: Action of G on a connected groupoid reconstructed from a group extension E of G by π, acting on a set Z with π acting freely. Each fibre B_g is a π-bitorsor, and objects are twisted by contracted products with B_g.
ideas.modern_name: equivalence between G-actions on connected groupoids and extensions with E-sets (semi-direct / extension dictionary; outer actions via bitorsors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. R. Brown's groupoid theory, Deligne 1989 (Galois action on groupoids with tangential base points), Ihara/Nakamura in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Bitorsors and contracted products are in Giraud / SGA-style torsor formalism; the specific equivalence is not to my knowledge in a published Grothendieck text

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine working-out of the standard dictionary between a group acting on a fundamental groupoid with several base points and an extension acting on the fibres of the universal cover. It is useful context for Grothendieck's multi-base-point / Teichmüller programme, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The page number '8' at the top right is the sheet number, not part of the text.
'Isom_{Π_1,f}(j,j')': the subscript after Π_1 is illegible; the meaning is simply Isom_{Π_1}(j,j') (morphisms in the groupoid).
In the bracket '[grâce à l'op. de E' sur X~'(I)]' the manuscript has J or I; it is consistent with J used elsewhere on the page.
Π_1 (the groupoid) is written with a doubled bold Π, distinct from the lower-case π_1 (the group); the transcription mostly preserves this.
